sources.title: Landmine Monitor 2025
sources.supports: 6,279 recorded casualties in 2024 (1,945 killed, 4,325 injured); 90% civilians; 46% children (1,701); 2,077 victim-activated improvised mines; 1,540 manufactured AP mines; underreporting of casualties; 2024 mine action funding US$1.07bn; Ukraine received $252.4m

sources.title: 2025 Landmine Monitor out now
sources.supports: 6,279 killed or injured in 2024, highest since 2020; 17 per day, almost half children; Myanmar 2,029, Syria 1,015, Afghanistan 624, Ukraine 293; 1,114 km2 land released and 105,640 AP mines destroyed in 2024; 166 treaty members

sources.title: Landmine Monitor 2025
sources.supports: Children account for nearly half of all landmine victims; global casualties at four-year high

sources.title: Clearing the Mines 2025 (report for the 22nd Meeting of States Parties to the Anti-Personnel Mine Ban Convention)
sources.supports: 175.39 km2 of AP mined area cleared globally in 2024 (vs 237.85 km2 in 2023, -26%); 131,190 AP mines destroyed in 2024 (-33%); 57 states/areas contaminated as of 1 Nov 2025; Afghanistan, Cambodia, Iraq, Ukraine massively contaminated (>100 km2)

sources.title: Pathways to Completion: Achieving A Common Goal Through Article 5 in Context
sources.supports: 33 States completed clearance since 1997 (as at 1 Nov 2024); stages of Article 5 implementation; survey vs clearance vs land release

sources.org: Geneva International Centre for Humanitarian Demining (GICHD)
sources.title: A Study of Mechanical Application in Demining
sources.supports: <3% of suspect areas cleared in 15 countries actually contained mines/UXO (area reduction is the biggest efficiency lever); manual clearance 1,600 m2 per 20-day cycle (80 m2/day) in high metal/heavy vegetation; MDD+manual 3,000 m2 per cycle (+87.5%); mechanical area reduction (SDTT) 22,400 m2 per 20 days + 22,400 m2 further reduced (+1,400% over manual, +2,100% counting second block); machines work only 3-4 hours/day; 23-person integrated team; HALO tractor up to 3,400 m2/day possible vs 560 m2/day actual, limited by manual demining rate of 500-600 m2/day; 190-lane study: manual productivity +73.8% mean (median +50%) after mechanical vegetation cutting, range 7-200%; metal contamination is the dominant driver; breaching lanes at 25% of area reduce a +50% gain to +37.5%; flail strike taxonomy (disruptive/detonation/ejection); magnets cost ~US$6,000; Abkhazia roller case: 49,000 m2 cleared manually vs 95,000 m2 cancelled out, cost +39% / productivity +323%; Thailand survey 933 areas / 2,560 km2 (3x prior Thai army estimate); flails are ground preparation, not stand-alone clearance

sources.org: CSIS Global Food and Water Security Program
sources.title: Demining Ukraine's Farmland: Progress, Adaptation, and Needs
sources.supports: Ukraine case: 470,000 ha designated in Mar 2023 action plan; 274,000 ha surveyed/cleared in 2023, 208,000 ha returned to farmers worth ~1 Mt wheat / USD 225m; 531,000 ha cleared and 439,000 ha returned by Oct 2024; 25,000 km2 agricultural land still contaminated (State Emergency Service), up to 8 M ha per GLOBSEC/Top Lead; 0 to 98 mechanical demining machines, 6 to 58 certified operators, 1,500 to 4,300 sappers; UAH 3 bn farmer compensation, Prozorro open auction gives 18% price drop saving UAH 44m over 11 auctions; USD 37 bn + 10,000 sappers needed (World Bank) for full demining; target 2033; >USD 1 bn pledged by allies; contamination suppresses GDP by USD 11.2 bn/yr (5.6% of 2021 GDP) and agricultural exports by USD 4.3 bn/yr (Tony Blair Institute); FAO/WFP found 2.75% of soils (~739 km2 of 24,000 km2) contaminated; domestic equipment production returns up to 40% of funding to Ukrainian businesses

sources.title: Cost of demining 1 ha of farmland stands at UAH 62,000 - MP Yuzhanina
sources.supports: UAH 62,000 per hectare to clear agricultural land, from 30 Prozorro auctions since start of 2025 covering 5,370 ha for a final cost of UAH 336.6 million; approx. UAH 1 trillion needed to clear all contaminated land in Ukraine; contaminated area 140,000 km2 at start of 2025; only UAH 2 billion allocated for mine clearance in the 2025 state budget

sources.org: Tony Blair Institute for Global Change (cited by CSIS)
sources.title: Economic impact assessment of landmine and ERW contamination in Ukraine
sources.supports: Contamination across all Ukrainian territory suppresses GDP by USD 11.2 billion annually (~5.6% of 2021 GDP); annual agricultural exports USD 4.3 billion lower than absent contamination

sources.title: Explosive Weapons Monitor 2025
sources.supports: More than 22,600 civilian fatalities from use of explosive weapons across 14,100+ incidents in 2025, a 21% decrease from more than 28,600 civilian deaths in 2024

sources.title: Explosive Weapons Monitor 2024
sources.supports: Gaza capture-recapture estimate of >64,000 direct traumatic-injury deaths (7 Oct 2023-30 Jun 2024), ~40% above the >41,900 reported; indirect deaths estimated at 3-15x direct deaths (up to 186,000+ in Gaza); media captured only ~1/3 of Gaza civilian deaths in Oct 2023; under-reporting of civilian fatalities is near-certain globally

sources.title: Explosive Violence Monitor 2024
sources.supports: 67,026 deaths and injuries from explosive weapons, 59,524 civilians (89%) - highest since 2010

sources.title: Explosive Violence Monitor 2025
sources.supports: 49,814 deaths and injuries from explosive weapons, 45,362 civilians (91%)
